nodes.name: MathematicalObject
nodes.definition: An abstract entity characterized by mathematical definitions and relations, independently of a concrete representation.

nodes.name: MathematicalExpression
nodes.definition: A structured symbolic expression denoting a mathematical object or operation under an interpretation.

nodes.name: MathematicalVariable
nodes.definition: A symbolic placeholder ranging over a declared mathematical domain; its symbol alone does not determine a value.

nodes.name: Numeral
nodes.definition: A symbolic representation of a number in a notation or numeral system.
examples: The symbols 10 written in a declared number base.
counterexamples: A numeral is a representation, not the number it denotes.

nodes.name: FractionExpression
nodes.definition: An expression representing division of a numerator by a nonzero denominator.

nodes.name: Percentage
nodes.definition: A real ratio expressed per hundred and interpreted relative to a stated reference quantity.

adaptation.reason: A percentage can be irrational; restriction to RationalNumber would exclude valid percentage values.

nodes.name: ComplexNumber
nodes.definition: A number expressible as a real component plus an imaginary component whose unit squares to minus one.

nodes.name: MathematicalSet
nodes.definition: An abstract collection determined by its elements; changing an element changes the set.

nodes.name: FiniteSet
nodes.definition: A mathematical set having a finite number of elements.

nodes.name: InfiniteSet
nodes.definition: A mathematical set that is not finite.

nodes.name: OrderedTuple
nodes.definition: A finite ordered sequence of entries for which positions and repeated values matter.

nodes.name: MathematicalFunction
nodes.definition: A mathematical mapping assigning exactly one output to each input in its declared domain; not a callable software implementation.
examples: The abstract squaring mapping.
counterexamples: A Python function implementing squaring is a software artifact.

nodes.name: Sequence
nodes.definition: A function indexed by an ordered discrete set, commonly integers or natural numbers.

nodes.name: ArithmeticSequence
nodes.definition: A numerical sequence with a constant difference between consecutive terms.

nodes.name: GeometricSequence
nodes.definition: A numerical sequence generated by multiplication by a fixed ratio between consecutive terms.

nodes.name: Polynomial
nodes.definition: An expression formed by finite sums of coefficients multiplied by nonnegative integer powers of variables.

nodes.name: AlgebraicEquation
nodes.definition: A formula expressing equality between algebraic expressions, with variables interpreted under an assignment or quantification.

adaptation.reason: An equation containing free variables is a formula whose truth depends on an assignment or quantification, not necessarily a complete proposition.

nodes.name: LinearEquation
nodes.definition: An algebraic equation of degree one in its unknown variables.

nodes.name: QuadraticEquation
nodes.definition: A single-variable polynomial equation whose highest nonzero degree is two.

nodes.name: MathematicalInequality
nodes.definition: A formula comparing ordered mathematical quantities using strict or nonstrict order, interpreted under an assignment or quantification.

adaptation.reason: An inequality may contain free variables and should not be treated as an asserted closed proposition merely by being represented.

nodes.name: LinearFunction
nodes.definition: A function preserving addition and scalar multiplication; school affine functions are separately represented.
examples: A transformation preserving addition and scalar multiplication.
counterexamples: The school expression y = 2x + 3 is affine and not linear in this definition.

nodes.name: AffineFunction
nodes.definition: A function consisting of a linear transformation plus a constant translation, including the school form y equals ax plus b.

nodes.name: QuadraticFunction
nodes.definition: A scalar function defined by a polynomial of degree two.

nodes.name: ExponentialFunction
nodes.definition: A function whose argument occurs in an exponent of a fixed positive base other than one.

nodes.name: LogarithmicFunction
nodes.definition: The inverse of a positive-base exponential function on its appropriate domain.

nodes.name: TrigonometricFunction
nodes.definition: A function relating an angle to ratios or coordinates defined by circular geometry.

nodes.name: GeometricFigure
nodes.definition: An abstract spatial configuration defined by points and geometric relations, distinct from a drawn representation.

nodes.name: GeometricPoint
nodes.definition: A zero-dimensional position in a geometric space.

nodes.name: GeometricLine
nodes.definition: A straight one-dimensional geometric figure extending without endpoints in both directions.

nodes.name: LineSegment
nodes.definition: The portion of a geometric line between and including two endpoints.

nodes.name: GeometricPlane
nodes.definition: A flat two-dimensional geometric space extending without boundary.

nodes.name: GeometricAngle
nodes.definition: A configuration of two rays with a common vertex, distinct from the quantity measuring their separation.

nodes.name: Polygon
nodes.definition: A closed plane figure bounded by a finite sequence of straight segments.

nodes.name: Triangle
nodes.definition: A polygon with three sides and three vertices.

nodes.name: Quadrilateral
nodes.definition: A polygon with four sides.

nodes.name: Rectangle
nodes.definition: A quadrilateral having four right angles.

nodes.name: Square
nodes.definition: A rectangle whose four sides have equal length.

nodes.name: Circle
nodes.definition: The set of points in a plane at a fixed distance from a center.
examples: The boundary at a fixed distance from a center.
counterexamples: The filled circular region is a disk.

nodes.name: GeometricDisk
nodes.definition: The region of a plane bounded by a circle, including its interior.

nodes.name: GeometricSolid
nodes.definition: A three-dimensional geometric figure considered with its occupied region.

nodes.name: Polyhedron
nodes.definition: A solid bounded by polygonal faces.

nodes.name: Prism
nodes.definition: A polyhedron with two congruent parallel polygonal bases and parallelogram lateral faces.

nodes.name: Pyramid
nodes.definition: A polyhedron formed by a polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at an apex.

nodes.name: Sphere
nodes.definition: The surface consisting of points at a fixed distance from a center in three-dimensional space.
examples: The two-dimensional surface of a geometric sphere.
counterexamples: Its three-dimensional interior belongs to a ball.

nodes.name: GeometricBall
nodes.definition: A solid region consisting of points whose distance from a center is at most a fixed radius.

nodes.name: Cylinder
nodes.definition: A solid generated by translating a planar base along a fixed direction outside the base plane.

nodes.name: Cone
nodes.definition: A solid formed by segments joining a planar base to a vertex outside its plane.

nodes.name: Vector
nodes.definition: An element of a vector space with defined vector addition and scalar multiplication.

nodes.name: Matrix
nodes.definition: A rectangular array of entries interpreted with specified dimensions and algebraic operations.

nodes.name: CoordinateSystem
nodes.definition: A convention assigning numerical coordinates to positions in a space relative to an origin and reference structure.

nodes.name: MathematicalLimit
nodes.definition: A value approached by a function or sequence under a specified limiting operation.

nodes.name: Derivative
nodes.definition: A function assigning an instantaneous rate of change where the appropriate difference-quotient limit exists.

nodes.name: Integral
nodes.definition: A mathematical value or function obtained by an integration operation with specified integrand and domain.

nodes.name: MathematicalProof
nodes.definition: A structured justification establishing a conclusion from stated axioms or premises by valid inference rules.

nodes.name: Theorem
nodes.definition: A proposition established within a specified formal or mathematical system by proof.

nodes.name: Axiom
nodes.definition: A proposition adopted as a starting assumption within a specified formal system.

nodes.name: PhysicalSystem
nodes.definition: A physical object or selected bounded portion of the world analyzed with declared components and environment.

nodes.name: PhysicalField
nodes.definition: A physical distribution assigning measurable properties across space and time, distinct from its mathematical representation.

nodes.name: PhysicalLaw
nodes.definition: A general empirical or theoretical proposition describing physical regularities within stated conditions and approximation limits.

nodes.name: Measurement
nodes.definition: An observation assigning a value to a quantity using an instrument, procedure, unit and conditions.

nodes.name: UnitSystem
nodes.definition: A coherent convention defining measurement units and their relations.

nodes.name: MeasurementUnit
nodes.definition: A defined reference magnitude used to express values of a measurement dimension.

nodes.name: AreaMeasure
nodes.definition: A dimensional quantity measuring two-dimensional extent.

nodes.name: VolumeMeasure
nodes.definition: A dimensional quantity measuring three-dimensional extent.

nodes.name: MassDensity
nodes.definition: Mass per unit volume under specified material and thermodynamic conditions.

nodes.name: Velocity
nodes.definition: The vector rate of change of position relative to a reference frame.

adaptation.reason: This quantity has vector values; the narrower source ConstantQuantity class assumes a scalar real magnitude. PhysicalQuantity avoids asserting scalar value semantics.

nodes.name: Speed
nodes.definition: The scalar magnitude of velocity relative to a reference frame.

nodes.name: Acceleration
nodes.definition: The rate of change of velocity relative to a reference frame.

adaptation.reason: This quantity has vector values; the narrower source ConstantQuantity class assumes a scalar real magnitude. PhysicalQuantity avoids asserting scalar value semantics.

nodes.name: Force
nodes.definition: A vector quantity describing an interaction that changes momentum under the selected physical model.

adaptation.reason: This quantity has vector values; the narrower source ConstantQuantity class assumes a scalar real magnitude. PhysicalQuantity avoids asserting scalar value semantics.

nodes.name: Momentum
nodes.definition: A dynamical quantity describing motion, equal to mass times velocity in elementary classical mechanics.

adaptation.reason: This quantity has vector values; the narrower source ConstantQuantity class assumes a scalar real magnitude. PhysicalQuantity avoids asserting scalar value semantics.

nodes.name: Energy
nodes.definition: A conserved physical quantity associated with the capacity for physical changes and transfers within a model.

nodes.name: KineticEnergy
nodes.definition: Energy associated with motion relative to a reference frame.

nodes.name: PotentialEnergy
nodes.definition: Energy associated with configuration in a specified interaction model and reference convention.

nodes.name: MechanicalWork
nodes.definition: Energy transferred by a force through displacement, computed with the relevant force-displacement relation.

nodes.name: Power
nodes.definition: The rate of energy transfer or conversion.

nodes.name: Pressure
nodes.definition: Normal force per unit area at a surface or within a medium.

nodes.name: ElectricCharge
nodes.definition: A conserved physical quantity determining electric interactions.

nodes.name: ElectricCurrent
nodes.definition: The rate of net electric charge flow through a specified cross-section.

nodes.name: Voltage
nodes.definition: Electric potential difference between two locations under a specified convention.

nodes.name: ElectricalResistance
nodes.definition: The voltage-to-current ratio for a component at specified operating conditions.

nodes.name: Frequency
nodes.definition: The number of cycles or repeated events per unit time for a specified phenomenon.

nodes.name: Wavelength
nodes.definition: The spatial period of a wave at a specified time and in a specified medium.

nodes.name: PhysicalMotion
nodes.definition: A change in position or configuration of physical entities relative to a frame.

nodes.name: TranslationalMotion
nodes.definition: Motion changing the position of an object without requiring a change of its orientation.

nodes.name: RotationalMotion
nodes.definition: Motion changing an object's orientation about an axis or center.

nodes.name: Oscillation
nodes.definition: Repeated variation about an equilibrium or recurring state.

nodes.name: WavePropagation
nodes.definition: Propagation of a disturbance or field variation through space or a medium.

nodes.name: HeatTransfer
nodes.definition: Energy transfer driven by temperature differences through conduction, convection or radiation.

nodes.name: ThermalConduction
nodes.definition: Heat transfer through microscopic interactions without bulk transport of material.

nodes.name: Convection
nodes.definition: Heat transfer involving bulk movement of a fluid.

nodes.name: ThermalRadiation
nodes.definition: Energy transfer by electromagnetic radiation associated with thermal emission and absorption.

nodes.name: PhaseTransition
nodes.definition: A change of the physical phase of matter under specified conditions.

nodes.name: Melting
nodes.definition: A transition from solid to liquid phase.

nodes.name: Evaporation
nodes.definition: Conversion of liquid to vapor at a liquid boundary.

nodes.name: Condensation
nodes.definition: Conversion from vapor to liquid phase.

nodes.name: ElectromagneticInduction
nodes.definition: Generation of an electromotive effect through changing magnetic flux or relative motion in an appropriate field.

nodes.name: LightReflection
nodes.definition: The return of incident light from a boundary into the medium from which it arrived.
examples: Light returning from a mirror.
counterexamples: Cognitive reflection is a separate process meaning.

nodes.name: LightRefraction
nodes.definition: A change in light propagation direction associated with changing optical propagation properties.

nodes.name: RadioactiveDecay
nodes.definition: A spontaneous transformation of an unstable atomic nucleus with emitted particles or radiation.

nodes.name: ChemicalElement
nodes.definition: A chemical species defined by a common number of protons in its atomic nuclei; distinct from a sample of elemental substance.

adaptation.reason: This meaning denotes a category of atoms defined by proton number rather than an individual physical material sample.

examples: The chemical species with proton number six.
counterexamples: A lump of graphite is a physical substance sample.

nodes.name: Isotope
nodes.definition: A nuclide category defined by proton number and neutron number; isotopes of an element differ in neutron count.

adaptation.reason: This meaning denotes a category of atoms defined by proton and neutron counts, not a single atom or material sample.

nodes.name: Ion
nodes.definition: An atom or bonded group of atoms carrying a net electric charge.

nodes.name: ChemicalBond
nodes.definition: A physical interaction holding atoms or ions together in a chemical structure.

nodes.name: CovalentBond
nodes.definition: A chemical bond characterized by shared electronic density between atoms.

nodes.name: IonicBond
nodes.definition: A chemical bonding interaction dominated by electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

nodes.name: ChemicalFormula
nodes.definition: A symbolic representation of the elemental composition or structure of a substance or chemical species.

nodes.name: ChemicalEquation
nodes.definition: A symbolic representation of reactants, products and stoichiometric relations in a chemical reaction.

nodes.name: ChemicalReaction
nodes.definition: A process changing chemical identities through rearrangement of atoms, electrons or chemical bonds.

nodes.name: Oxidation
nodes.definition: A chemical process involving electron loss or an increase in oxidation state under the chosen representation.

nodes.name: ChemicalReduction
nodes.definition: A chemical process involving electron gain or a decrease in oxidation state under the chosen representation.

nodes.name: AcidBaseReaction
nodes.definition: A reaction involving proton transfer or another explicitly stated acid-base definition.

nodes.name: Combustion
nodes.definition: An exothermic oxidation reaction producing rapid energy release under suitable conditions.

nodes.name: ChemicalSolution
nodes.definition: A homogeneous mixture with solute dispersed at molecular or ionic scale in a solvent.

nodes.name: Acid
nodes.definition: A substance acting as a proton donor or acid under a declared acid-base model and conditions.

nodes.name: ChemicalBase
nodes.definition: A substance acting as a proton acceptor or base under a declared acid-base model and conditions.

nodes.name: Salt
nodes.definition: An ionic compound composed of cations and anions, with identity determined by its constituents and structure.

nodes.name: OrganicCompound
nodes.definition: A carbon-containing compound classified within organic chemistry under stated conventions, commonly with carbon-hydrogen frameworks.

nodes.name: Hydrocarbon
nodes.definition: An organic compound containing only carbon and hydrogen.

nodes.name: Alcohol
nodes.definition: An organic compound bearing a hydroxyl group bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

nodes.name: Carbohydrate
nodes.definition: A saccharide or related organic compound serving structural, energy-storage or metabolic functions.

nodes.name: Lipid
nodes.definition: An organic compound in the broad biochemical group characterized by hydrophobic or amphipathic behavior.

nodes.name: Protein
nodes.definition: A biological polymer or complex built from amino acid residues linked into polypeptide chains.

nodes.name: NucleicAcid
nodes.definition: A polymer of nucleotides involved in biological information storage, transfer or function.

nodes.name: DNA
nodes.definition: A nucleic acid using deoxyribose units and commonly carrying hereditary sequence information.

nodes.name: RNA
nodes.definition: A nucleic acid using ribose units with informational, structural, regulatory or catalytic functions.

nodes.name: AmountOfSubstance
nodes.definition: A quantity proportional to the count of specified elementary entities, commonly expressed in moles.

nodes.name: ChemicalConcentration
nodes.definition: A quantity expressing the amount of a constituent relative to a specified amount or extent of a mixture.

nodes.name: AcidityMeasure
nodes.definition: A quantitative measure of acid-related behavior under a stated definition, such as pH for an aqueous solution.

nodes.name: BiologicalStructure
nodes.definition: A structural part of an organism considered by its composition, organization or biological function.

nodes.name: Cell
nodes.definition: A membrane-bounded structural and functional biological unit, whether free living or part of an organism.

nodes.name: CellMembrane
nodes.definition: A selective boundary enclosing a cell and regulating interactions with its environment.

nodes.name: Organelle
nodes.definition: A specialized subcellular structure performing particular functions.

nodes.name: CellNucleus
nodes.definition: A membrane-enclosed compartment containing most genomic DNA in a eukaryotic cell.

nodes.name: Mitochondrion
nodes.definition: A eukaryotic organelle involved in cellular energy conversion and other metabolic functions.

nodes.name: Chloroplast
nodes.definition: A photosynthetic organelle of plants and some eukaryotic algae.

nodes.name: Tissue
nodes.definition: An organized group of cells and associated material forming a structural or functional unit.

nodes.name: Organ
nodes.definition: A differentiated body structure composed of tissues and carrying out coordinated biological functions.

nodes.name: OrganSystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated set of organs participating in related bodily functions.

nodes.name: Gene
nodes.definition: A genomic sequence region contributing to a functional product or inherited regulatory function under a stated gene model.

nodes.name: Chromosome
nodes.definition: An organized DNA-containing structure carrying genomic material.

nodes.name: Animal
nodes.definition: A multicellular eukaryotic organism in the animal lineage, typically obtaining nutrition by consuming organic material.

nodes.name: Vertebrate
nodes.definition: An animal belonging to the lineage characterized by a vertebral column or its developmental homologues.

nodes.name: Invertebrate
nodes.definition: An animal outside the vertebrate grouping; this is a practical grouping rather than a single evolutionary clade.

nodes.name: Mammal
nodes.definition: A vertebrate of the mammalian lineage characterized by mammary glands and associated inherited traits.

nodes.name: Human
nodes.definition: An organism of the species Homo sapiens; social roles and mental states do not define separate human biological classes.

adaptation.reason: SUMO lists Hominid, CognitiveAgent. The profile selects local.hominid as the single primary inclusion route and does not create extra inheritance facts.

nodes.name: Bird
nodes.definition: A vertebrate in the avian lineage, characterized by feathers and related inherited traits.

nodes.name: Reptile
nodes.definition: A cold-blooded vertebrate of the conventional source reptile grouping, with scales or horny plates and lungs; this source meaning excludes birds.
examples: A member of the source conventional ectothermic reptile grouping.
counterexamples: Cladistic usage including birds must use a separate meaning; this source profile does not assert sibling disjointness.

nodes.name: Amphibian
nodes.definition: A vertebrate in the amphibian lineage, commonly undergoing aquatic and terrestrial life stages.

nodes.name: Fish
nodes.definition: An aquatic gill-bearing vertebrate in the conventional non-tetrapod fish grouping, which is not a single clade.

nodes.name: Arthropod
nodes.definition: An invertebrate with a segmented body, jointed appendages and an external skeleton.

nodes.name: Insect
nodes.definition: An arthropod in the insect lineage, typically with three body regions and three pairs of adult legs.

nodes.name: Mollusc
nodes.definition: An invertebrate of the molluscan lineage, typically with a mantle and muscular foot.

nodes.name: Plant
nodes.definition: An organism in the plant lineage; photosynthesis is common but not a universal defining requirement.

nodes.name: FloweringPlant
nodes.definition: A plant in the angiosperm lineage that produces flowers and seeds enclosed in fruits.

nodes.name: Conifer
nodes.definition: A seed plant in the conifer lineage, typically producing seeds in cones.

nodes.name: Fern
nodes.definition: A vascular plant in the fern lineage reproducing by spores rather than seeds.

nodes.name: Moss
nodes.definition: A nonvascular land plant in the moss lineage.

nodes.name: Fungus
nodes.definition: A eukaryotic organism in the fungal lineage, commonly obtaining nutrients through absorption.

nodes.name: Bacterium
nodes.definition: A cellular organism belonging to the bacterial domain of life.

nodes.name: Archaeon
nodes.definition: A cellular organism belonging to the archaeal domain of life.

nodes.name: Protist
nodes.definition: A eukaryotic organism grouped conventionally outside animals, land plants and fungi; the grouping is not a single clade.

nodes.name: Virus
nodes.definition: An acellular infectious biological entity that replicates through host cellular machinery; this profile does not settle whether viruses count as organisms.
examples: An acellular infectious entity using host replication machinery.
counterexamples: An executable malicious program belongs to software, not this biological meaning.

nodes.name: BiologicalPopulation
nodes.definition: A spatiotemporally scoped collection of organisms of the same species or an explicitly defined reproductive grouping.
examples: Organisms of a specified species in a specified area and period.
counterexamples: The word population in a statistical model need not denote organisms.

nodes.name: BiologicalCommunity
nodes.definition: A collection of interacting populations occupying a specified environment and time range.

nodes.name: Ecosystem
nodes.definition: A system comprising organisms and their abiotic environment with interacting flows and processes.

nodes.name: FoodChain
nodes.definition: A representation of sequential feeding and energy-transfer relations among organisms or trophic groups.

nodes.name: Habitat
nodes.definition: A spatial environment occupied by an organism or population, characterized relative to its living requirements and temporal scope.

adaptation.reason: A habitat may be outside Earth or in an artificial setting; the source GeographicArea meaning is restricted to three-dimensional Earth regions.

nodes.name: BiologicalSpecies
nodes.definition: A category of organisms delimited by an explicitly stated biological, phylogenetic or other species criterion.
examples: A class delimited by an explicit species criterion.
counterexamples: A local herd is a population collection, not a species.

nodes.name: Metabolism
nodes.definition: The coordinated chemical transformations sustaining an organism or cell.

nodes.name: Photosynthesis
nodes.definition: Biological conversion of light energy into chemical energy with synthesis of organic compounds.

nodes.name: CellularRespiration
nodes.definition: Biological transfer of energy from substrates through cellular oxidation and associated pathways.

nodes.name: Digestion
nodes.definition: Breakdown and processing of food into forms available for biological use.

nodes.name: BiologicalReproduction
nodes.definition: Production of new organisms or biological reproductive units.

nodes.name: CellDivision
nodes.definition: A biological process in which a cell gives rise to daughter cells.

nodes.name: Mitosis
nodes.definition: Eukaryotic nuclear division distributing replicated chromosomes into daughter nuclei.

nodes.name: Meiosis
nodes.definition: A nuclear division process reducing chromosome complement in sexual reproduction.

nodes.name: BiologicalInheritance
nodes.definition: Transmission of biological information or traits from predecessors to descendants.

nodes.name: GeneticMutation
nodes.definition: A change in the sequence or organization of genetic material.

nodes.name: NaturalSelection
nodes.definition: Differential reproduction or survival associated with heritable variation in a population under specified conditions.

nodes.name: BiologicalEvolution
nodes.definition: Change in inherited characteristics of populations across generations.

nodes.name: HomeostaticRegulation
nodes.definition: Regulation maintaining relevant biological variables within viable ranges despite disturbances.

nodes.name: ImmuneResponse
nodes.definition: Coordinated biological activity recognizing and responding to perceived pathogens or abnormal material.

nodes.name: Planet
nodes.definition: A planetary body identified under a stated astronomical classification, distinct from its political regions or map representations.

nodes.name: Star
nodes.definition: A self-gravitating astronomical body producing substantial energy through nuclear fusion during part of its evolution.

nodes.name: NaturalSatellite
nodes.definition: A naturally occurring body orbiting a larger astronomical body.

nodes.name: Continent
nodes.definition: A major terrestrial landmass recognized under an explicit geographical convention.

nodes.name: Island
nodes.definition: A land area surrounded by water at the relevant reference water level.

nodes.name: Peninsula
nodes.definition: A land area projecting into water while remaining connected to a larger land area.

nodes.name: Mountain
nodes.definition: A substantially elevated landform relative to its surrounding terrain under a geographical convention.

nodes.name: Plain
nodes.definition: A land area with relatively low relief over a substantial extent.

nodes.name: Valley
nodes.definition: An elongated low area between higher terrain, often associated with drainage.

nodes.name: Desert
nodes.definition: A geographic area characterized by low precipitation and related ecological conditions, not necessarily high temperature.

nodes.name: Forest
nodes.definition: A geographic area dominated by trees under a stated canopy or ecological criterion.

nodes.name: Ocean
nodes.definition: A major connected body or conventionally delimited division of planetary saline water.

nodes.name: Sea
nodes.definition: A substantial saline water body or named division of an ocean under geographical convention.

nodes.name: River
nodes.definition: A natural flowing watercourse with a channel, catchment and temporally varying flow.

nodes.name: Lake
nodes.definition: An inland body of standing water within a geographic basin.

nodes.name: Glacier
nodes.definition: A persistent land-based mass of ice formed from accumulated snow and moving under its own weight.

adaptation.reason: A glacier in this meaning is a structured physical ice body, not the geographic region that it occupies.

nodes.name: Atmosphere
nodes.definition: The gaseous envelope surrounding a celestial body and interacting with its surface and space environment.

nodes.name: Hydrosphere
nodes.definition: The collection of water in its relevant phases and reservoirs on or near a planetary body.

nodes.name: PlanetaryCrust
nodes.definition: The outer solid structural layer of a planetary body.

nodes.name: TectonicPlate
nodes.definition: A relatively rigid lithospheric portion moving in relation to neighboring plates.

nodes.name: Rock
nodes.definition: A naturally formed geological material composed of minerals or mineraloids.

nodes.name: Mineral
nodes.definition: A naturally occurring geological substance classified by composition and ordered internal structure under mineralogical criteria.

nodes.name: Soil
nodes.definition: A near-surface mixture of mineral material, organic matter, water, gases and organisms supporting terrestrial processes.

nodes.name: WeatherState
nodes.definition: The atmospheric condition at a specified location and time or short interval.
examples: Atmospheric conditions in a city this afternoon.
counterexamples: A multi-decade statistical summary belongs to climate description.

nodes.name: ClimateDescription
nodes.definition: A statistical characterization of weather over a specified region, period and baseline convention.

nodes.name: AtmosphericPrecipitation
nodes.definition: The fall of water in liquid or solid form from the atmosphere toward a surface.

nodes.name: Wind
nodes.definition: Bulk motion of atmospheric gas relative to a planetary surface.

nodes.name: WaterCycle
nodes.definition: Circulation of water among atmospheric, surface, subsurface and biological reservoirs through multiple physical processes.

nodes.name: Erosion
nodes.definition: Removal and transport of geological material by water, wind, ice or related physical agents.

nodes.name: Earthquake
nodes.definition: A seismic occurrence involving sudden release of energy in a planetary crust or interior.

nodes.name: VolcanicEruption
nodes.definition: An occurrence in which magma, gas or fragmented material escapes through a volcanic system.

nodes.name: Flood
nodes.definition: Inundation of land normally not covered by water under a stated local baseline.

nodes.name: GeographicCoordinate
nodes.definition: A coordinate specifying location relative to a geographic reference system and datum.

nodes.name: Map
nodes.definition: A spatial representation of selected features using projection, scale, symbols and a reference system.

nodes.name: MapScale
nodes.definition: The ratio between represented distance on a map and corresponding ground distance under stated projection conditions.

adaptation.reason: A length ratio need not be rational; RealNumber preserves the intended geometric meaning without a false rationality constraint.

nodes.name: TimeZone
nodes.definition: A geographic area using a specified convention for civil time during a specified period.

nodes.name: MentalState
nodes.definition: A temporally scoped condition of a mind, specified through an applicable psychological model and evidence.

nodes.name: Emotion
nodes.definition: A coordinated affective condition involving appraisal, experience and bodily or behavioral tendencies under a psychological model.
examples: A person's fear of a particular perceived threat during an interval.
counterexamples: A model output saying fear is not evidence that the model has a human emotional state.

nodes.name: Fear
nodes.definition: An emotional condition organized around perceived threat or danger.

nodes.name: Anger
nodes.definition: An emotional condition often involving perceived obstruction, injury or injustice and a tendency toward confrontation.

nodes.name: Joy
nodes.definition: A positively valenced emotional condition associated with valued experiences or appraisals.

nodes.name: Sadness
nodes.definition: An emotional condition commonly associated with loss or disappointment and reduced activation.

nodes.name: Surprise
nodes.definition: An emotional response to an event violating expectations; it does not by itself imply positive or negative value.

nodes.name: StressState
nodes.definition: A scoped psychological condition arising when perceived demands tax or exceed perceived coping resources.

nodes.name: Mood
nodes.definition: A relatively diffuse affective condition extending beyond a single clearly bounded eliciting event.

nodes.name: MotivationState
nodes.definition: A scoped condition organizing the initiation, direction or persistence of behavior toward valued outcomes.

nodes.name: Intention
nodes.definition: An agent commitment or readiness to perform a course of action, distinct from performance or success.
examples: An agent intention to run a check.
counterexamples: An intended check is not an executed or successful check.

nodes.name: PsychologicalAttitude
nodes.definition: A learned evaluative disposition toward an entity or topic, distinguishable from a single immediate emotional state.

nodes.name: PersonalityTrait
nodes.definition: A comparatively enduring tendency in patterns of thought, feeling or behavior, assessed with model and context limitations.

nodes.name: Temperament
nodes.definition: A disposition in emotional reactivity or self-regulation with substantial developmental and biological influences.

nodes.name: PsychologicalNeed
nodes.definition: A condition or requirement relevant to psychological functioning under an explicitly stated theory.

nodes.name: SelfConcept
nodes.definition: A person's psychological representation of who they are, including self-ascribed characteristics, social roles and identity, shaped by experience and interpretation.

adaptation.reason: The unrestricted self-representation meaning duplicated AgentSelfModel. This psychological meaning is narrower and therefore specializes the shared generic representation instead of repeating it.

examples: A person describing themselves as a learner and as a member of a community.
counterexamples: A software agent capability registry is a generic self-model, not evidence of this human psychological self-concept.

nodes.name: SelfEfficacy
nodes.definition: An agent expectation of its capability to perform a particular action in a specified context.

nodes.name: Habit
nodes.definition: A learned behavioral disposition cued by context and expressed with reduced deliberative demand.

nodes.name: SocialNorm
nodes.definition: A shared expectation or prescription concerning behavior within a specified social group and context.

nodes.name: SocialIdentity
nodes.definition: An individual representation of membership in and significance of social groups.

nodes.name: SocialInfluence
nodes.definition: A social process affecting another agent's judgments, behavior or experience.

nodes.name: Cooperation
nodes.definition: Interaction in which participants coordinate contributions toward compatible or shared goals.

nodes.name: SocialConflict
nodes.definition: Interaction involving incompatible interests, goals or perceived claims between agents.

nodes.name: Communication
nodes.definition: An intentional interaction expressing or exchanging content through a medium and an interpretive context.

nodes.name: Persuasion
nodes.definition: Communication intended to change another agent's attitude, belief or intention.

nodes.name: Negotiation
nodes.definition: Communication seeking an agreement among parties with potentially different interests.

nodes.name: InterpersonalAttachment
nodes.definition: An enduring emotional bond involving a particular other individual, distinct from biological kinship or legal guardianship.

nodes.name: EmpathicProcess
nodes.definition: A process of understanding or sharing another's perspective or affect while retaining a distinction between self and other.

nodes.name: PsychologicalDevelopment
nodes.definition: Change in psychological capacities, organization or behavior across an organism's life and environment.

nodes.name: Sleep
nodes.definition: A regulated biological process involving characteristic changes in responsiveness, behavior and physiology.

nodes.name: Organization
nodes.definition: A socially constituted collection of participating agents coordinated by rules, roles and goals, with an identity that can survive membership change.
examples: A university retaining identity across changes of staff.
counterexamples: The general institution of education is a system of practices.

nodes.name: SocialInstitution
nodes.definition: A persistent system of socially established rules, roles and practices governing a domain of interaction; distinct from a particular organization.

nodes.name: Government
nodes.definition: An organization or coordinated set of organs exercising public governing authority over a jurisdiction.

nodes.name: Company
nodes.definition: An organization constituted for economic activity under a specified legal or institutional regime.

nodes.name: NonprofitOrganization
nodes.definition: An organization whose governing regime restricts distribution of surplus to owners as private profit.

nodes.name: EducationalOrganization
nodes.definition: An organization with an institutional purpose of providing education or instruction.

nodes.name: ResearchOrganization
nodes.definition: An organization whose activities include systematic production and evaluation of knowledge.

nodes.name: PoliticalParty
nodes.definition: An organization seeking political influence or governmental representation through coordinated political activity.

nodes.name: InternationalOrganization
nodes.definition: An organization constituted across national jurisdictions by states or other participants under a stated charter.

nodes.name: SocialCommunity
nodes.definition: A collection of people connected by sustained interaction, shared setting or shared social identification.

nodes.name: Household
nodes.definition: A socially or statistically defined unit of people sharing residence or household arrangements for a stated purpose.

nodes.name: FamilyGroup
nodes.definition: A social group organized around recognized kinship, caregiving or partnership relations under a stated context.

nodes.name: Country
nodes.definition: A geopolitical territory identified by an applicable political or geographic convention; sovereignty and recognition require separate claims.
examples: A territory described under a stated geographical convention.
counterexamples: Recognition and sovereignty are separate claims, not consequences of the name.

nodes.name: JurisdictionArea
nodes.definition: A geographic scope within which a stated authority or legal regime applies during a specified period.

nodes.name: City
nodes.definition: An urban settlement recognized as a city under a specified administrative or geographic convention.

nodes.name: Settlement
nodes.definition: A geographic area of established human habitation, including urban and rural forms.

nodes.name: GeopoliticalBorder
nodes.definition: A spatial boundary delimiting territories under a specified source, time and recognition context.

nodes.name: LegalNorm
nodes.definition: A rule recognized as legally relevant within a specified jurisdiction, authority and period; validity is a scoped claim.

nodes.name: LegalInstrument
nodes.definition: A formally expressed legal text or instrument issued, agreed or adopted under a legal process.

nodes.name: Constitution
nodes.definition: A foundational legal instrument specifying a political community's governing arrangements and fundamental norms.

nodes.name: Statute
nodes.definition: A legislative legal instrument enacted by a competent lawmaking body in a jurisdiction.

nodes.name: Regulation
nodes.definition: A legal instrument containing rules issued by a body under a stated regulatory authority.

nodes.name: Contract
nodes.definition: An agreement intended to establish legally relevant commitments between parties under an applicable legal regime.

nodes.name: CourtDecision
nodes.definition: A formal determination produced by a court in a proceeding with specified jurisdiction and legal effects.

nodes.name: LegalRight
nodes.definition: A legally recognized entitlement or protected position held by a subject within a specified regime and scope.

nodes.name: LegalObligation
nodes.definition: A legally grounded requirement on a subject to act or refrain from acting under specified conditions.

nodes.name: LegalLiability
nodes.definition: A subject's legally grounded exposure to an obligation, sanction or remedy under specified facts and jurisdiction.

nodes.name: LegalPersonRole
nodes.definition: The status of being recognized as a bearer of legal rights and duties in a specified legal regime.

nodes.name: PublicLaw
nodes.definition: A body of legal doctrine and norms concerning public authority and its relations under a stated legal system.

nodes.name: PrivateLaw
nodes.definition: A body of legal doctrine and norms concerning relations among private subjects under a stated legal system.

nodes.name: ConstitutionalLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning constitutional structures, powers and fundamental protections.

nodes.name: AdministrativeLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law governing public administration, its powers, procedures and review.

nodes.name: CriminalLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law defining offenses, criminal responsibility and authorized punishments within a jurisdiction.

nodes.name: CivilLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning private rights, obligations and remedies; this meaning excludes the civil-law legal-system family.
examples: Private rights and remedies in a specified jurisdiction.
counterexamples: The civil-law legal-system tradition is a distinct sense.

nodes.name: CommercialLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning commercial transactions and business relations.

nodes.name: LaborLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning work and employment relationships, often spanning private and public norms.

nodes.name: FamilyLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning legally recognized family relationships and associated rights and obligations.

nodes.name: TaxLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning public taxation, assessment, collection and related duties.

nodes.name: IntellectualPropertyLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning rights over protected creative, technical or identifying subject matter.

nodes.name: PrivacyLaw
nodes.definition: A body of law concerning protection and permitted processing of personal information and private life.

nodes.name: InternationalLaw
nodes.definition: A body of legal norms governing international relations and other cross-border subjects under stated sources and scope.

nodes.name: Court
nodes.definition: An institutionally constituted organization authorized to adjudicate matters within a jurisdiction.

nodes.name: LegalProceeding
nodes.definition: An organized process for applying or determining legal rules, facts or remedies under procedural authority.

nodes.name: Election
nodes.definition: A collective selection process using voting under declared eligibility and counting rules.

nodes.name: LegislationProcess
nodes.definition: A process of proposing, deliberating, adopting or amending legal instruments through a legislative authority.

nodes.name: PublicPolicy
nodes.definition: An articulated course of public action or guiding rule adopted or proposed by public authorities.

nodes.name: PoliticalIdeology
nodes.definition: A system of political values, explanations and prescriptions concerning social organization and authority.

nodes.name: PoliticalPower
nodes.definition: A capacity of an agent or institution to influence collective decisions or behavior in a political context.

nodes.name: Sovereignty
nodes.definition: A claimed or recognized position of supreme governing authority within a scope, dependent on legal and political context.

nodes.name: War
nodes.definition: A sustained organized armed conflict classified under explicit historical, political or legal criteria.

nodes.name: Diplomacy
nodes.definition: Communication and negotiation among political representatives concerning collective external relations.

nodes.name: EconomicTransaction
nodes.definition: An interaction transferring or committing economically relevant resources, rights or obligations between parties.

nodes.name: Purchase
nodes.definition: A transaction agreeing an exchange of a good, service or right for payment; agreement does not by itself establish delivery.
examples: Agreement to exchange an item for a price.
counterexamples: Purchase agreement alone does not entail delivery, ownership transfer or payment completion.

nodes.name: Payment
nodes.definition: A transfer of monetary value intended to discharge or advance an obligation under specified conditions.

nodes.name: EmploymentRelationship
nodes.definition: A scoped relationship in which a person provides labor under agreed terms and an applicable institutional regime.

nodes.name: MarketInstitution
nodes.definition: An institutional arrangement through which offers, demand and exchange for a category of goods or services are coordinated.

nodes.name: MonetaryInstrument
nodes.definition: A physical token or implemented instrument used as a medium of payment or monetary value under an institutional convention.

nodes.name: CurrencySystem
nodes.definition: An institutional system specifying a monetary unit and conventions for monetary valuation and payment.

nodes.name: Price
nodes.definition: A monetary amount offered, agreed or observed for a specified item, quantity, time and transaction conditions.

nodes.name: Cost
nodes.definition: A monetary valuation of resources consumed or foregone for a specified activity under a stated accounting boundary.

nodes.name: Income
nodes.definition: A monetary flow accruing to a subject during a stated period under a specified accounting definition.

nodes.name: Profit
nodes.definition: A monetary difference between defined revenue and expense flows for a period under an accounting convention.

nodes.name: AssetRole
nodes.definition: The role of a resource treated as controlled economic value for a subject under a stated accounting or economic definition.

nodes.name: DebtObligation
nodes.definition: An obligation to transfer monetary value or another specified resource to a creditor under stated terms.

nodes.name: FinancialInstrument
nodes.definition: A contractual or legally recognized instrument creating financial rights and obligations.

nodes.name: EquityShare
nodes.definition: A financial instrument representing an ownership interest under the issuer's governing regime.

nodes.name: DebtSecurity
nodes.definition: A transferable financial instrument representing a debt obligation under stated payment terms.

nodes.name: Budget
nodes.definition: A plan allocating expected resources, revenues and expenditures over a defined period or activity.

nodes.name: InflationRate
nodes.definition: A rate of change in a specified price index over a stated period and population of items.

nodes.name: GrossDomesticProduct
nodes.definition: An aggregate monetary measure of production within an economy over a period under a specified national-accounts definition.

nodes.name: UnemploymentRate
nodes.definition: The ratio of persons classified as unemployed to a specified labor-force population at a time or period.

nodes.name: SupplyChain
nodes.definition: A scoped collection of participating organizations and resources linked through production and delivery activities.

nodes.name: NewsReport
nodes.definition: A report presenting selected events or claims as news with identifiable sources, publication time and editorial framing.
examples: An attributed report with a publication date and cited sources.
counterexamples: Repeated syndication does not provide independent evidence.

nodes.name: Claim
nodes.definition: A proposition presented by a source as asserted within a context; being a claim does not establish truth.
examples: A source assertion whose truth is to be assessed.
counterexamples: A claim node is not automatic endorsement.

nodes.name: Opinion
nodes.definition: An expressed judgment or evaluation attributed to a source and context, distinguished from directly observed fact.

nodes.name: Rumor
nodes.definition: A circulating claim whose source or verification status is uncertain in the stated context.

nodes.name: SourceReport
nodes.definition: A content item reporting observations, assertions or analysis with an attributable source and production context.

nodes.name: PressRelease
nodes.definition: A report issued by an organization or representative for public dissemination of its position or announcement.

nodes.name: PublicEvent
nodes.definition: An occurrence of public relevance or accessibility under a stated community and context.

nodes.name: Disaster
nodes.definition: An occurrence causing severe disruption and harm relative to a community's capacity and stated criteria.

nodes.name: Transportation
nodes.definition: A process moving people or goods between locations with stated participants and route conditions.

nodes.name: Vehicle
nodes.definition: A device designed to convey people or goods between locations.

nodes.name: Building
nodes.definition: A constructed structure providing enclosed or sheltered space for human activities or storage.

nodes.name: Dwelling
nodes.definition: A building designed or used as living accommodation under a stated use context.

nodes.name: Room
nodes.definition: A spatial subdivision of a building delineated for occupancy or use.

nodes.name: FoodMaterial
nodes.definition: Material suitable or intended for ingestion as nourishment for a specified kind of organism and conditions.

nodes.name: Meal
nodes.definition: An organized episode of eating by an agent, possibly with other agents and social conventions.

adaptation.reason: A meal can be eaten alone and therefore does not universally entail social interaction.

nodes.name: Cooking
nodes.definition: Preparation of food through selected transformations such as heating, mixing or preservation.

nodes.name: Cleaning
nodes.definition: Removal of unwanted material from an object or environment under a stated cleanliness criterion.

nodes.name: PhysicalMaintenance
nodes.definition: Activities preserving or restoring the functioning of physical objects under a maintenance objective.

nodes.name: Travel
nodes.definition: Purposeful movement of an agent between locations over an episode.

nodes.name: AppointmentPlan
nodes.definition: An agreement or plan for participants to engage in an activity at a specified time and context.

nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.definition: An arrangement assigning activities or commitments to times or temporal constraints.

nodes.name: LocationDescription
nodes.definition: Information specifying a location relative to a reference system, context and precision.

nodes.name: Address
nodes.definition: A conventional locator for a physical place or delivery destination under an addressing scheme.

nodes.name: ResourceRole
nodes.definition: The role of an entity as available means for achieving a stated purpose within constraints.

nodes.name: OwnerRole
nodes.definition: A role established by a scoped ownership relation under a legal, institutional or personal convention.
examples: Ownership scoped to an asset, regime and time.
counterexamples: Temporary possession alone is not ownership.

nodes.name: CustomerRole
nodes.definition: The role of a party seeking, acquiring or receiving goods or services in a transaction context.

nodes.name: ProviderRole
nodes.definition: The role of a party supplying goods, services or access in a specified interaction.

nodes.name: CaregiverRole
nodes.definition: The role of an agent providing care to another under a scoped personal or institutional relationship.

nodes.name: LegalGuardianRole
nodes.definition: A legally established role authorizing duties or decisions for another person under a specific jurisdiction and interval.
examples: Guardianship assigned by a relevant legal process for an interval.
counterexamples: A guardian need not be a biological parent.

nodes.name: BiologicalParentRole
nodes.definition: The role of an organism in a biological parentage relation under a stated reproductive criterion.

nodes.name: AvailabilityState
nodes.definition: A condition specifying whether an entity can be accessed or used for a purpose during an interval.

nodes.name: OwnershipState
nodes.definition: A temporal condition of an entity concerning who holds an ownership relation under stated conventions.

nodes.name: HealthState
nodes.definition: A scoped condition of an organism's functioning assessed under a stated health model and evidence.
examples: A scoped condition supported by observations of an organism.
counterexamples: Low evidence confidence is not itself a disease condition.

nodes.name: DiseaseCondition
nodes.definition: A health condition characterized by an abnormal functional or structural pattern under a stated medical classification.

nodes.name: WarmBloodedVertebrate
nodes.definition: A vertebrate whose body temperature is internally regulated within a relatively stable range under typical physiological conditions.

nodes.name: ColdBloodedVertebrate
nodes.definition: A vertebrate whose body temperature is not internally regulated in the conventional source grouping.

nodes.name: Primate
nodes.definition: A mammal in the primate lineage, including humans and other primates.

nodes.name: Hominid
nodes.definition: A primate in the SUMO grouping comprising humans and their relatively recent ancestors; this adopted source sense is not the broader modern great-ape family label.
counterexamples: Do not silently equate this source sense with every current biological use of Hominidae.

nodes.name: AnatomicalStructure
nodes.definition: A structure of an organism's body with a particular biological organization or function.

nodes.name: BodyPart
nodes.definition: An anatomical structure that is a part of an organism's body.

nodes.name: ArithmeticOperation
nodes.definition: A mathematical function transforming a permitted tuple of numerical inputs into a numerical result under a declared number system.

nodes.name: Addition
nodes.definition: An arithmetic operation combining numerical inputs according to the additive structure of the declared number system.

nodes.name: Subtraction
nodes.definition: An arithmetic operation producing the difference of ordered numerical inputs where that difference is defined.

nodes.name: Multiplication
nodes.definition: An arithmetic operation combining numerical inputs according to the multiplicative structure of the declared number system.

nodes.name: Division
nodes.definition: An arithmetic operation finding a quotient for ordered inputs on a domain that excludes undefined divisors.
counterexamples: Division by zero is outside the ordinary real-number operation domain.

nodes.name: Exponentiation
nodes.definition: An arithmetic operation assigning a power to a base and exponent on a domain where the value is defined.

nodes.name: AbsoluteValue
nodes.definition: A function assigning a nonnegative magnitude to a number under the chosen number system, such as distance from zero for real numbers.

nodes.name: PositiveInteger
nodes.definition: An integer strictly greater than zero.

nodes.name: PrimeNumber
nodes.definition: An integer greater than one with exactly two positive integer divisors.

nodes.name: CompositeNumber
nodes.definition: An integer greater than one with a positive divisor other than one and itself.

nodes.name: EvenInteger
nodes.definition: An integer divisible by two without a remainder.

nodes.name: OddInteger
nodes.definition: An integer whose remainder on division by two is one under the standard integer convention.

nodes.name: GeometricTransformation
nodes.definition: A mapping from points of a geometric space to points of a geometric space under a specified rule.

nodes.name: GeometricTranslation
nodes.definition: A transformation moving every point by the same vector.

nodes.name: GeometricRotation
nodes.definition: A distance-preserving geometric transformation rotating points about a specified center or axis.

nodes.name: GeometricReflection
nodes.definition: A geometric transformation mapping points to their mirror positions relative to a specified line, plane or other declared reference.
examples: Mapping a figure to its mirror image about a line.
counterexamples: Light reflection is a physical process; cognitive reflection is a reasoning process.

nodes.name: ElectricField
nodes.definition: A physical field describing the electric force per unit test charge under stated frame and model conditions.

nodes.name: MagneticField
nodes.definition: A physical field describing magnetic effects on moving charges and magnetic moments under a stated model.

nodes.name: GravitationalField
nodes.definition: A physical field describing gravitational influence, with the mathematical interpretation stated by the applicable theory.

nodes.name: FrictionForce
nodes.definition: A force associated with interaction at a contact interface opposing relative motion or its tendency under stated conditions.

nodes.name: ElasticForce
nodes.definition: A force associated with deformation and tending to restore a material system toward a reference configuration within an elastic regime.

nodes.name: BuoyantForce
nodes.definition: The resultant force due to a pressure distribution in a surrounding fluid under stated conditions.

nodes.name: ElectricalCircuit
nodes.definition: A connected physical arrangement of components providing paths and conditions for electrical behavior.

nodes.name: Resistor
nodes.definition: An electrical device designed to provide resistance over specified operating conditions.

nodes.name: Capacitor
nodes.definition: An electrical device designed to store energy through separated charge and an electric field.

nodes.name: Inductor
nodes.definition: An electrical device designed to store energy in a magnetic field associated with current.

nodes.name: ElectrochemicalBattery
nodes.definition: A device using one or more electrochemical cells to supply electrical energy.

nodes.name: OpticalLens
nodes.definition: An optical device directing light primarily by refraction through shaped transmissive material.

nodes.name: CatalystRole
nodes.definition: The role of a substance in changing a reaction rate through a pathway in which the catalyst is regenerated overall; the role is reaction- and condition-specific.
examples: A material catalyzing one specified reaction under controlled conditions.
counterexamples: A material name alone does not establish catalytic function for every reaction.

nodes.name: ReactantRole
nodes.definition: The role of a chemical species or material consumed or transformed in a specified reaction description.

nodes.name: ReactionProductRole
nodes.definition: The role of a chemical species or material produced in a specified reaction description.

nodes.name: Brain
nodes.definition: A centralized organ of the nervous system coordinating information processing and physiological or behavioral functions in an organism.

nodes.name: Heart
nodes.definition: A biological organ that pumps circulatory fluid through a circulatory system.

nodes.name: Lung
nodes.definition: An internal respiratory organ supporting gas exchange with an external gaseous environment.

nodes.name: Kidney
nodes.definition: An organ involved in regulating fluid and chemical balance and excreting metabolic waste in relevant animals.

nodes.name: PlantRoot
nodes.definition: A plant organ commonly anchoring the organism and absorbing water and dissolved materials from its environment.

nodes.name: PlantLeaf
nodes.definition: A plant organ commonly specialized for photosynthesis, gas exchange or related functions.

nodes.name: Flower
nodes.definition: A reproductive organ of an angiosperm plant containing structures involved in sexual reproduction.

nodes.name: NervousSystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated biological system transmitting and processing signals through nervous tissue.

nodes.name: CirculatorySystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated organ system transporting circulatory fluid and associated substances through an organism.

nodes.name: RespiratorySystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated organ system supporting gas exchange between an organism and its environment.

nodes.name: DigestiveSystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated organ system processing food and absorbing usable nutrients.

nodes.name: EndocrineSystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated biological system regulating functions through hormones and their producing organs or tissues.

nodes.name: SkeletalSystem
nodes.definition: A coordinated set of structural body elements supporting the organism and associated movement or protection.
